children.title: Farkas Lemma Family
children.top_down_role: Linear and conic alternatives organized around multiplier certificates.

locator_traceability.matched_excerpt: - 2.3.1. Polyhedral Cones and Farkas' Lemma p. 102

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_r,c\in\mathbb R^n\), let \(A\) have columns \(a_i\), and let \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_r\}=\{A\lambda:\lambda\geq0\}\). Use the polar convention \(K^\circ=\{z:\langle z,k\rangle\leq0\ \forall k\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional, finitely generated cones and equivalent finite linear systems. The family groups equality, inequality, homogeneous-polar, and qualified conic forms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Farkas lemma family is the collection of certificate systems obtained from the canonical cone-membership alternative \(c\in K\), equivalently \(\exists\lambda\geq0\) with \(A\lambda=c\), versus \(\exists z\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(A^Tz\leq0\) and \(c^Tz>0\). Its homogeneous consequence form is \([a_i^Tz\leq0\ \forall i]\Rightarrow c^Tz\leq0\) if and only if \(c\in K\). Equality- and inequality-system forms arise by representing unrestricted variables as differences and equations as paired inequalities. A member of the family is identified by its primal sign restrictions, its multiplier cone, the adjoint cancellation equation, and the strict scalar separation inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Farkas family consists of equivalent linear alternatives organized around membership in a finitely generated cone. The primal asks whether c is a nonnegative combination of the generators. The certificate is a vector whose inner product is nonpositive with every generator but strictly positive with c. The same relation can be written as a consequence theorem for homogeneous inequalities or transformed into equality- and inequality-system feasibility alternatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(c\in\operatorname{cone}\{a_i\}\iff [A^Tz\leq0\Rightarrow c^Tz\leq0]\), with infeasibility certificate \(A^Tz\leq0,\ c^Tz>0\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: The polar identity is \(K^{\circ\circ}=K\), because a finitely generated cone is closed.
For \(A\lambda=c,\lambda\geq0\), infeasibility is certified by \(A^Tz\leq0\) and \(c^Tz>0\).
For \(Ax\leq b\), infeasibility is certified by \(y\geq0\), \(A^Ty=0\), and \(b^Ty<0\).
special_cases_latex: Taking \(c=0\) yields homogeneous cone and dependence forms, but strict separation must be formulated carefully because \(0\in K\).
Taking \(K=\mathbb R_+^r\) recovers nonnegative multiplier geometry.
immediate_consequences_latex: Any valid homogeneous linear consequence of finitely many homogeneous inequalities has nonnegative multiplier coefficients.
Every infeasible finite equality system with nonnegative variables admits a separating linear functional.
boundary_notes: For a nonclosed cone, bipolarity gives \(K^{\circ\circ}=\overline K\), so exact membership cannot be inferred without closedness.
Sign conventions vary across sources; reversing the polar convention reverses all displayed inequalities simultaneously.

children.title: Equality-System Farkas Forms
children.top_down_role: Alternative formulations centered on linear equations and sign restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Equality-System Infeasibility Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An infeasible nonnegative equality system has a Farkas multiplier whose pairing with the right-hand side is normalized to minus one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), the system \(Ax=b\), \(x\ge0\), is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \[A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y=-1.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists x\ge0:Ax=b\iff\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y=-1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixing the negative pairing at minus one removes the irrelevant positive scaling of a strict Farkas certificate.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Separation Is Essential
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A non-strict certificate condition is invalid because the zero multiplier can coexist with a feasible primal system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Replacing \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) in the equality-form Farkas alternative by \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\) destroys exclusivity. For \(A=[1]\) and \(b=1\), the primal system has the feasible solution \(x=1\), while \(y=0\) simultaneously satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\ge0:Ax=b\) and \(\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\) both hold.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This example isolates why a strictly negative pairing, or its normalized equivalent, is required for an exclusive alternative.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Free-and-Nonnegative Equality Alternative
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For equations with free and nonnegative variables, infeasibility is certified by a multiplier orthogonal to the free-variable columns, nonnegative on the nonnegative-variable columns, and strictly negative on the right-hand side.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A_F\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times p}\), \(A_N\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times q}\), and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\). Exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \[A_Fu+A_Nv=b,\qquad u\in\mathbb{R}^p,\quad v\in\mathbb{R}_+^q;\] or \[A_F^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad A_N^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y<0.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists(u,v):A_Fu+A_Nv=b,\ v\ge0\) and \(\exists y:A_F^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ A_N^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This is the equality-system Farkas variant with free and nonnegative variable blocks; the seed is recovered when the free block is absent.

knowledge_statements.title: Equality-System Farkas Forms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Either Ax=b has a nonnegative solution, or a linear functional separates b from the cone generated by A's columns, but not both.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax=b\) with \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\); or \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) with \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The second system is therefore a verifiable certificate that the equality system has no nonnegative solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x\ge0:Ax=b\) and \(\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas alternative for nonnegative solutions of linear equations.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\). The primal variable \(x\) is constrained componentwise by \(x\geq0\); the multiplier \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite equality systems with nonnegative primal variables. This is the cone-membership form of Farkas' lemma.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The equality-system Farkas form associated with \((A,b)\) is the pair \(\mathsf P_{=}(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=b,\ x\geq0\}\) and \(\mathsf C_{=}(A,b)=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:A^Ty\leq0,\ b^Ty>0\}\). Thus \(x\) represents \(b\) as a nonnegative combination of the columns of \(A\), while \(y\) separates \(b\) from their generated cone. The defining validity relation is exclusive exactness: precisely one of \(\mathsf P_{=}(A,b)\) and \(\mathsf C_{=}(A,b)\) is nonempty. Under the opposite polar convention one may replace \(y\) by \(-y\), obtaining \(A^Ty\geq0\) and \(b^Ty<0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equality system with nonnegative variables, the primal witness is x≥0 satisfying Ax=b. The alternative certificate is an unrestricted vector y satisfying Aᵀy≤0 and bᵀy>0. Geometrically, the columns of A generate a cone, the primal asserts that b belongs to it, and the certificate strictly separates b from that cone. Exactly one witness type exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf P_{=}(A,b)=\{x\geq0:Ax=b\}\), \(\mathsf C_{=}(A,b)=\{y:A^Ty\leq0,\ b^Ty>0\}\), and exactly one is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(b\in A\mathbb R_+^n\) versus \(\exists y\) with \(\sup_{k\in A\mathbb R_+^n}y^Tk\leq0<y^Tb\).
Using \(u=-y\), the certificate conditions become \(A^Tu\geq0\) and \(b^Tu<0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\), feasibility holds exactly when \(b=0\); otherwise a separating \(y\) can be chosen parallel to \(b\).
If \(b\) is a column of \(A\), the corresponding coordinate vector is a primal witness.
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasibility question is exactly membership of \(b\) in the polyhedral cone generated by the columns of \(A\).
A certificate remains valid after multiplication by any positive scalar.
boundary_notes: Dropping \(x\geq0\) changes the primal image from a cone to the column space and changes the certificate to \(A^Ty=0\).
The strict inequality \(b^Ty>0\) is essential for separating nonmembership from boundary membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Inequality-System Farkas Forms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear inequality system is infeasible exactly when a nonnegative combination of its rows cancels the variables and makes the right side negative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax\le b\) for some \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\); or \(y\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x:Ax\le b\) and \(\exists y\ge0:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Farkas alternative for a system of non-strict inequalities.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and interpret \(Ax\leq b\) componentwise. The primal variable is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite systems containing only weak linear inequalities over the real numbers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The inequality-system Farkas form is the exact alternative pair \(\mathsf P_{\leq}(A,b)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\leq b\}\) and \(\mathsf C_{\leq}(A,b)=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:y\geq0,\ A^Ty=0,\ b^Ty<0\}\). The nonnegative multiplier restriction preserves the directions of the primal inequalities, the equation \(A^Ty=0\) eliminates the unrestricted variable, and \(b^Ty<0\) supplies strict contradiction. Precisely one of these sets is nonempty. Equality rows may be included by replacing each equality by two opposite inequalities, or equivalently by allowing its associated multiplier to be unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a finite weak-inequality system Ax≤b, a primal certificate is any feasible x. An infeasibility certificate is a nonnegative vector y that cancels the variable coefficients through Aᵀy=0 and has negative aggregated right-hand side bᵀy. Exactly one of the primal and certificate systems is feasible. Equality constraints can be represented by paired inequalities or by unrestricted multipliers.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\{x:Ax\leq b\}\) and \(\{y:y\geq0,\ A^Ty=0,\ b^Ty<0\}\) is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: With rows \(a_i^T\), a certificate is \(y_i\geq0\) satisfying \(\sum_i y_i a_i=0\) and \(\sum_i y_i b_i<0\).
Under the reversed inequality convention \(Ax\geq b\), the corresponding form is \(y\geq0\), \(A^Ty=0\), and \(b^Ty>0\).
special_cases_latex: For a single inequality \(a^Tx\leq\beta\) with \(a\neq0\), the primal set is always nonempty and no certificate exists.
A negative constant row \(0^Tx\leq\beta<0\) gives an immediate one-row certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: The positive support of \(y\) selects an infeasible subsystem.
After normalizing a nonzero certificate by \(\mathbf1^Ty=1\), certificate search becomes a polyhedral feasibility problem.
boundary_notes: Mixed strict and weak inequalities require Motzkin-type alternatives rather than this form.
If floating-point tolerances replace exact inequalities, strict negativity of \(b^Ty\) must not be silently weakened to nonpositivity.

children.top_down_role: Origin-centered alternatives and cone membership.

knowledge_statements.title: Homogeneous Farkas Forms
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear functional is nonpositive on a homogeneous inequality cone exactly when it is a nonnegative combination of the defining rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^n\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax\le0\) and \(c^{\mathsf T}x>0\) for some \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\); or \(A^{\mathsf T}y=c\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\). Hence the homogeneous implication \(Ax\le0\Rightarrow c^{\mathsf T}x\le0\) holds precisely when \(c\) is a nonnegative combination of the rows of \(A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x:Ax\le0,\ c^{\mathsf T}x>0\) and \(\exists y\ge0:A^{\mathsf T}y=c\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous inequality form of the Farkas alternative.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Homogeneous Consequence and Polar-Cone Farkas Form
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(a_1,\ldots,a_m,a_0\in\mathbb R^n\), and let \(K=\operatorname{cone}\{a_1,\ldots,a_m\}\). All right-hand sides are zero.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Origin-centered homogeneous inequalities and finitely generated cone membership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous Farkas form associates the system \(a_i^Tx\leq0\) for \(i=1,\ldots,m\) with the consequence inequality \(a_0^Tx\leq0\). The consequence is valid for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying the system exactly when there exists \(\lambda\in\mathbb R_+^m\) such that \(a_0=\sum_{i=1}^m\lambda_i a_i\). Equivalently, \(a_0\in K^{\circ\circ}=K\), where \(K^\circ=\{x:a_i^Tx\leq0\ \forall i\}\). A separating failure certificate for \(a_0\notin K\) is an \(x\) satisfying \(a_i^Tx\leq0\) for every \(i\) and \(a_0^Tx>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The homogeneous Farkas form asks when one zero-right-hand-side inequality follows from finitely many others. The consequence a₀ᵀx≤0 holds for every x satisfying aᵢᵀx≤0 exactly when a₀ is a nonnegative linear combination of the vectors aᵢ. Equivalently, a₀ lies in the bipolar of their finitely generated cone. Failure is witnessed by a vector satisfying all premise inequalities while strictly violating the claimed consequence.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \([a_i^Tx\leq0\ \forall i]\Rightarrow a_0^Tx\leq0\ \forall x\iff\exists\lambda\geq0:\ a_0=\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(a_0\in K\iff a_0\in K^{\circ\circ}\).
Exactly one holds: \(a_0\in K\), or \(\exists x\in K^\circ\) with \(a_0^Tx>0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(a_0=0\), the consequence is valid with \(\lambda=0\).
If \(m=1\), validity means \(a_0\) is a nonnegative scalar multiple of \(a_1\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every valid homogeneous linear consequence has a nonnegative multiplier representation.
Redundant homogeneous inequalities correspond to generators lying in the cone of the remaining normals.
boundary_notes: The conclusion concerns implication for every \(x\), not feasibility of the homogeneous premise, which always contains \(x=0\).
For infinitely generated or nonclosed cones, the bipolar yields closure and may certify only membership in \(\overline K\).

children.title: Conic Farkas Extension
children.top_down_role: Extension from orthant geometry to general closed convex cones.

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Cone Conic Farkas Alternative
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When the conic image plus a residual cone is closed, either the conic inclusion is feasible or an adjoint dual-cone vector strictly certifies infeasibility, but not both.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(Q\subset\mathbb R^m\) be closed convex cones, let \(A:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R^m\) be linear, and assume \(A(K)+Q\) is closed. For every \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), exactly one of the following holds: \[\exists x\in K,\ q\in Q:\ Ax+q=b;\] \[\exists y\in\mathbb R^m:\ A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\ y\in Q^*,\ \langle y,b\rangle<0.\]
assumptions_latex: \(K\subset\mathbb R^n\) and \(Q\subset\mathbb R^m\) are closed convex cones.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(b\in A(K)+Q\) and \(\exists y\in Q^*:\ A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\ \langle y,b\rangle<0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-cone form containing the seed equality form as the case \(Q=\{0\}\).

notation.meaning: Feasible image cone including conic residuals

knowledge_statements.title: Conic Farkas Extension
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under closedness of the conic image, failure of Ax=b with x in K has a separator whose adjoint lies in the dual cone.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be a closed convex cone, let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), and assume that \(A(K)\) is closed. For every \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), exactly one system is feasible: \(Ax=b\) with \(x\in K\); or \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*\) and \(b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\), where \(K^*=\{z:\langle z,x\rangle\ge0\text{ for all }x\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x\in K:Ax=b\) and \(\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y\in K^*,\ b^{\mathsf T}y<0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic Farkas lemma with closed-image qualification.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a nonempty closed convex cone, \(K^*=\{y:\langle y,k\rangle\geq0\ \forall k\in K\}\), \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic linear inequalities. Exact infeasibility certification is distinguished from certification of failure of approximate feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The conic Farkas certificate system for \(Ax-b\in K\) is \(\mathsf P_K(A,b)=\{x:Ax-b\in K\}\) and \(\mathsf C_K(A,b)=\{y\in K^*:A^Ty=0,\ b^Ty>0\}\). Every \(y\in\mathsf C_K(A,b)\) certifies \(\mathsf P_K(A,b)=\varnothing\). Moreover, \(\mathsf C_K(A,b)\neq\varnothing\) exactly when \(b\notin\overline{A\mathbb R^n-K}\), equivalently when the conic system is not approximately feasible. If \(A\mathbb R^n-K\) is closed, then exact infeasibility and non-approximate feasibility coincide, so precisely one of \(\mathsf P_K(A,b)\) and \(\mathsf C_K(A,b)\) is nonempty. This closed-image qualification is part of the exact conic extension.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a closed convex cone K, the primal conic system requires Ax−b to belong to K. A certificate is a dual-cone vector y that annihilates A and has positive inner product with b. Such a vector always proves infeasibility. It exists exactly when b lies outside the closure of the conic image Aℝⁿ−K. Consequently, the usual exact alternative holds when that image is closed; without this qualification, an infeasible but approximately feasible system may have no certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf P_K(A,b)=\{x:Ax-b\in K\}\), \(\mathsf C_K(A,b)=\{y\in K^*:A^Ty=0,\ b^Ty>0\}\), and \(\mathsf C_K(A,b)\neq\varnothing\iff b\notin\overline{A\mathbb R^n-K}\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Approximate feasibility is \(b\in\overline{A\mathbb R^n-K}\).
Under closedness of \(A\mathbb R^n-K\), infeasibility is equivalent to existence of \(y\in K^*\) with \(A^Ty=0\) and \(b^Ty>0\).
special_cases_latex: For \(K=\mathbb R_+^m\), the image is polyhedral and closed, recovering the ordinary finite linear alternative.
For \(K=\{0\}\), feasibility is \(Ax=b\), and certificates lie in \(\ker A^T\) with \(b^Ty>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: A conic multiplier certificate is stable under positive scaling.
Polyhedral cones inherit exact Farkas alternatives because the relevant linear-conic image is polyhedral and closed.
boundary_notes: Closedness of \(K\) alone does not guarantee closedness of \(A\mathbb R^n-K\).
Nonpolyhedral cones can admit infeasible but approximately feasible systems for which both the primal and strict certificate systems are empty.

notation.meaning: Dual cone under the nonnegative pairing convention.
Conic feasibility image containing b exactly when the primal is feasible.

children.title: Gordan Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous strict alternatives associated with positive orthant geometry.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). Strict vector inequalities are componentwise, and \(\mathbb R_{++}^m=\{u:u_i>0\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous strict systems and nonnegative dependence certificates in finite-dimensional real spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The homogeneous Gordan alternative associated with \(A\) is the pair \(\mathsf G_P(A)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax<0\}\) and \(\mathsf G_C(A)=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:y\geq0,\ y\neq0,\ A^Ty=0\}\). Exactly one set is nonempty. The Gordan theorem family consists of this pair, its sign-reversed form \(Ax>0\) versus the same nonnegative dependence system, and inhomogeneous strict-image formulations \(Ax<b\) characterized by the absence of nonzero \(y\geq0\) satisfying \(A^Ty=0\) and \(b^Ty\leq0\). The common structural feature is strict feasibility of a linear image paired with a nonzero orthant multiplier annihilating that image.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The canonical Gordan alternative pairs a strictly negative homogeneous image Ax<0 with a nonzero nonnegative dependence y satisfying Aᵀy=0. Exactly one exists. Reversing A gives the strictly positive image version. The broader family also includes strict affine systems Ax<b, whose obstruction is a nonzero nonnegative annihilating multiplier with nonpositive pairing against b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x:Ax<0\) and \(\exists y\geq0:\ y\neq0,\ A^Ty=0\) holds.
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(A)\cap(-\mathbb R_{++}^m)\neq\varnothing\) if and only if \(\ker(A^T)\cap(\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\).
For \(Ax>0\), replace \(A\) by \(-A\); the certificate system is unchanged.
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\) and \(m>0\), no strict image exists and every nonzero \(y\geq0\) is a certificate.
For a single row \(a^T\neq0\), a strict image exists and the certificate set is empty.
immediate_consequences_latex: A nonnegative dependence certificate can be normalized to \(\mathbf1^Ty=1\).
The alternative depends only on the range of \(A\) and the orthogonal subspace \(\ker A^T\).
boundary_notes: Replacing strict positivity by nonnegativity yields a different alternative.
The inhomogeneous condition contains the additional scalar restriction \(b^Ty\leq0\); it must not be dropped.

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Margin Form of Strict Positive-Image Feasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A homogeneous linear image contains a strictly positive vector exactly when it contains a vector whose every coordinate is at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \[\exists x\in\mathbb R^n\;Ax>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists u\in\mathbb R^n\;Au\ge\mathbf1.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\;Ax>0\iff\exists u\;Au\ge\mathbf1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous normalization of componentwise strict positivity to a closed unit-margin system.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict Positive-Image Alternatives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear image contains a strictly positive vector exactly when the rows admit no nonzero nonnegative dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax>0\) for some \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\); or \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) for some nonzero \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x:Ax>0\) and \(\exists y\ge0:y\ne0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gordan's strict positive-image alternative.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), let \(L=\operatorname{range}(A)\), and let \(\mathbb R_{++}^m=\operatorname{int}\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous strict positivity in every image coordinate; partial or weak positivity is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A strict positive-image witness is an \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(Ax\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\), equivalently \(Ax>0\). Its alternative certificate is a vector \(y\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\) satisfying \(A^Ty=0\). The strict positive-image alternative is the exclusive relation \(L\cap\mathbb R_{++}^m\neq\varnothing\) exactly when \(L^\perp\cap(\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\). Thus strict coordinatewise positivity of some linear image is paired with absence of a nontrivial nonnegative functional that vanishes on the entire image subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strict positive-image witness is a vector x for which every coordinate of Ax is positive. The obstruction is a nonzero nonnegative vector y orthogonal to every vector in the image of A, equivalently Aᵀy=0. Exactly one of these possibilities holds. In subspace language, the range of A meets the open positive orthant precisely when its orthogonal complement contains no nonzero point of the closed nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax>0\iff\ker(A^T)\cap(\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb R_{++}^m\neq\varnothing\iff L^\perp\cap\mathbb R_+^m=\{0\}\).
Exactly one holds: \(Ax>0\) for some \(x\), or \(A^Ty=0\) for some \(0\neq y\geq0\).
special_cases_latex: If \(L=\mathbb R^m\), a strict positive image exists and \(L^\perp=\{0\}\).
If \(L=\{0\}\) and \(m>0\), no strict positive image exists and every nonzero nonnegative vector is a certificate.
immediate_consequences_latex: Surjectivity of \(A\) is sufficient, but not necessary, for strict positive-image feasibility.
A certificate may be normalized to the simplex \(\{y\geq0:\mathbf1^Ty=1\}\).
boundary_notes: The open orthant \(\mathbb R_{++}^m\) cannot be replaced by \(\mathbb R_+^m\) without changing the alternative.
Requiring only one positive component is a different feasibility regime.

knowledge_statements.title: Normalized Nonnegative Dependence Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positive-image infeasibility is equivalent to a nonnegative row-dependence certificate normalized so that its entries sum to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), the system \(Ax>0\) is infeasible if and only if there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(y\ge0\), \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), and \(\mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}y=1\). Equivalently, every nonzero nonnegative dependence certificate can be scaled to lie in the probability simplex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nexists x\in\mathbb{R}^n:Ax>0\iff\exists y\ge0:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ \mathbf{1}^{\mathsf T}y=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Soundness, completeness, and simplex normalization of the certificate side of Gordan's theorem.

notation.meaning: Every component of Ax is strictly positive.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonnegative Dependence Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Infeasibility of Ax>0 is certified by a nonzero nonnegative vector giving a zero-weighted dependence among A's rows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Ax>0\) has no solution for \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), then there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\setminus\{0\}\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m_+\setminus\{0\}:A^{\mathsf T}y=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate side of Gordan's theorem.

children.top_down_role: Separation of a linear subspace from a positive orthant.

knowledge_statements.title: Gordan Cone-Subspace Geometry
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A subspace either meets the strictly positive orthant or has a nonzero nonnegative vector in its orthogonal complement, exclusively.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) be a linear subspace. Exactly one of the following alternatives holds: \(L\cap\mathbb{R}^m_{++}\ne\varnothing\); or \(L^\perp\cap(\mathbb{R}^m_+\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\). Thus a subspace misses the strictly positive orthant precisely when its orthogonal complement contains a nonzero nonnegative normal. Taking \(L=\operatorname{range}(A)\) recovers Gordan's matrix alternative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(L\cap\mathbb{R}^m_{++}\ne\varnothing\) and \(L^\perp\cap(\mathbb{R}^m_+\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric subspace–orthant form of Gordan's theorem.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(L\subseteq\mathbb R^m\) be a linear subspace, let \(P=\mathbb R_{++}^m\), let \(P^*=\mathbb R_+^m\), and let \(L^\perp=\{y:y^Tz=0\ \forall z\in L\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric subspace formulation of the homogeneous Gordan alternative in a finite-dimensional Euclidean space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Gordan cone-subspace configuration is the pair \((L,P)\) together with the two witness sets \(\mathsf W(L)=L\cap P\) and \(\mathsf S(L)=L^\perp\cap(P^*\setminus\{0\})\). A vector in \(\mathsf W(L)\) is a strict positive-orthant intersection witness. A vector in \(\mathsf S(L)\) defines a hyperplane through the origin that contains \(L\) and is nonnegative on the closed positive orthant. The configuration satisfies the exclusive relation \(\mathsf W(L)\neq\varnothing\iff\mathsf S(L)=\varnothing\). For a matrix representation \(L=\operatorname{range}(A)\), the sets become \(\{Ax:Ax>0\}\) and \(\{y\geq0:y\neq0,A^Ty=0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The geometric Gordan configuration consists of a linear subspace and the open positive orthant. One witness is a strictly positive point belonging to the subspace. The alternative witness is a nonzero nonnegative vector orthogonal to the subspace; its orthogonal hyperplane contains the subspace and supports the positive orthant at the origin. The subspace meets the open orthant exactly when no such nonzero orthogonal nonnegative vector exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb R_{++}^m\neq\varnothing\iff L^\perp\cap(\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: If \(L=\operatorname{range}(A)\), then \(L^\perp=\ker A^T\).
The obstruction hyperplane is \(H_y=\{z:y^Tz=0\}\), where \(L\subseteq H_y\) and \(y^Tk>0\) for every \(k\in\mathbb R_{++}^m\).
special_cases_latex: For \(L=\mathbb R^m\), the intersection witness set is nonempty and \(L^\perp=\{0\}\).
For \(L=\{0\}\), the intersection witness set is empty and every nonzero \(y\geq0\) is a separating witness.
immediate_consequences_latex: The alternative depends only on the subspace, not on a particular matrix whose range equals it.
The separating normal may be normalized to lie in the standard simplex.
boundary_notes: The hyperplane generally supports the closed orthant at the origin; it need not strictly separate the subspace from every boundary point of the orthant.
Replacing the open orthant by the closed orthant changes the geometric statement.

children.top_down_role: Kernel and row-space alternatives involving strict positivity.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(c\in\mathbb R^m\). Write \(x>0\) for componentwise strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional equality systems with strictly positive variables and their transposed sign certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Stiemke transposition family is centered on the positive equality system \(\mathsf P_S(A,c)=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax=c,\ x>0\}\). Its transposed sign condition is \(A^Ty\geq0\) and \(c^Ty\leq0\). The system is Stiemke-feasible exactly when every \(y\in\mathbb R^m\) satisfying those two inequalities also satisfies the equalities \(A^Ty=0\) and \(c^Ty=0\). Equivalently, infeasibility is certified by some \(y\) with \(A^Ty\geq0\), \(c^Ty\leq0\), and at least one of \(A^Ty\) or \(c^Ty\) nonzero. The family includes the homogeneous case \(c=0\), where positive kernel vectors are paired with nonzero nonnegative row-space vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stiemke’s family concerns equality systems Ax=c with every component of x strictly positive. Feasibility is equivalent to the following transposed condition: whenever Aᵀy is nonnegative and cᵀy is nonpositive, both quantities must actually vanish. Thus infeasibility is witnessed by a y satisfying the sign conditions with at least one strict nonzero outcome. For c=0 this becomes the positive-kernel versus row-space-sign alternative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x>0:Ax=c\iff\forall y,\ [A^Ty\geq0,\ c^Ty\leq0\Rightarrow A^Ty=0,\ c^Ty=0]\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Infeasibility is equivalent to \(\exists y\) such that \(A^Ty\geq0\), \(c^Ty\leq0\), and \((A^Ty,c^Ty)\neq(0,0)\).
For \(c=0\), feasibility becomes \(\ker A\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\neq\varnothing\), and the obstruction is a nonzero vector in \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)\cap\mathbb R_+^n\).
special_cases_latex: If \(c=0\), the statement is the homogeneous positive-kernel alternative.
If \(A\) is square and invertible, feasibility is equivalent to \(A^{-1}c>0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The homogeneous alternative depends only on the row space of \(A\).
Any inhomogeneous obstruction is invariant under positive scaling of \(y\).
boundary_notes: Strict positivity of every component of \(x\) is essential; allowing zero components gives a different alternative.
The certificate is not merely \(A^Ty\geq0\); the scalar condition \(c^Ty\leq0\) is required in the inhomogeneous case.

children.title: Positive-Kernel Alternatives
children.top_down_role: Homogeneous feasibility regimes involving positive kernel vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Closed Linear-Feasibility Normalization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A strictly positive kernel vector exists exactly when a kernel vector exists whose every component is at least one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \[\exists x>0:Ax=0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists u\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:Au=0,\quad u\ge\mathbf 1.\] Thus positive-kernel feasibility has an equivalent closed linear-feasibility formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:Ax=0,\ x>0\}\ne\varnothing\iff\{u:Au=0,\ u\ge\mathbf1\}\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent closed polyhedral formulation of strictly positive kernel feasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Kernel Alternatives
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matrix has a strictly positive kernel vector exactly when its row space contains no nonzero nonnegative vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every matrix \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), exactly one of the following systems is feasible: \(Ax=0\) with \(x>0\); or \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\) for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x>0:Ax=0\) and \(\exists y:A^{\mathsf T}y\ge0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\ne0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stiemke's alternative for a strictly positive kernel vector.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\). The positive orthant is \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), the nonnegative orthant is \(\mathbb R_+^n\), and \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)=(\ker A)^\perp\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The homogeneous \(c=0\) specialization of Stiemke transposition, distinguished from Gordan's positive-image alternative by exchanging kernel and range roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive-kernel witness is a vector \(x\in\ker A\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\), that is, \(Ax=0\) and \(x_i>0\) for every coordinate. A row-space sign certificate is a vector \(s=A^Ty\in\mathbb R_+^n\setminus\{0\}\) for some \(y\in\mathbb R^m\). The positive-kernel alternative is the exclusive relation \(\ker A\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\neq\varnothing\) exactly when \(\operatorname{range}(A^T)\cap(\mathbb R_+^n\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\). Equivalently, exactly one of \(Ax=0,\ x>0\) and \(A^Ty\geq0,\ A^Ty\neq0\) has a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-kernel witness is a strictly positive vector annihilated by A. Its alternative certificate is a nonzero nonnegative vector lying in the row space of A, written as Aᵀy. Exactly one exists. This is the homogeneous Stiemke alternative and differs from Gordan’s positive-image form because strict positivity is sought in the kernel, while the sign certificate lies in the row space.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker A\cap\mathbb R_{++}^n\neq\varnothing\iff\operatorname{range}(A^T)\cap(\mathbb R_+^n\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\).
equivalent_formulations_latex: Exactly one system is feasible: \(Ax=0,\ x>0\); or \(A^Ty\geq0,\ A^Ty\neq0\).
Every \(y\) satisfying \(A^Ty\geq0\) must satisfy \(A^Ty=0\) if and only if a positive-kernel witness exists.
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\), every \(x>0\) is a positive-kernel witness and the row-space certificate set is empty.
If \(\ker A=\{0\}\) and \(n>0\), no positive-kernel witness exists, so a nonzero nonnegative row-space certificate exists.
immediate_consequences_latex: The alternative is invariant under elementary row operations on \(A\), since they preserve its kernel and row space.
A positive-kernel witness may be normalized by \(\mathbf1^Tx=1\), turning it into a point in the relative interior of the simplex.
boundary_notes: Replacing \(x>0\) by \(x\geq0\), \(x\neq0\), produces a different boundary-sensitive alternative.
The certificate vector is \(A^Ty\), not necessarily the multiplier \(y\) itself; no sign restriction is imposed on \(y\).

notation.meaning: Set of strictly positive kernel witnesses.

children.title: Row-Space Sign Certificates
children.top_down_role: Sign-structured row-space witnesses of positive-kernel infeasibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex-Normalized Row-Space Certificate
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero nonnegative row-space witness exists exactly when one exists whose coordinates sum to one.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \[\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n}_{+}\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists\widehat y\in\mathbb{R}^{m}:A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=1.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})\cap(\mathbb{R}^{n}_{+}\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\iff\exists\widehat y:A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y\ge0,\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}A^{\mathsf T}\widehat y=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Scale-fixed normalization of Stiemke's nonnegative row-space witness.

knowledge_statements.title: Row-Space Sign Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-kernel infeasibility is certified by a nonzero nonnegative vector belonging to the row space of A.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(Ax=0\), \(x>0\), is infeasible for \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), then there exists \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\}\). Such an adjoint image is a row-space sign certificate of positive-kernel infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m:A^{\mathsf T}y\in\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Certificate side of Stiemke's theorem.

notation.meaning: Row space of \(A\), represented as adjoint images.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\). Its row space is \(\mathcal R(A^{\mathsf T})=\{A^{\mathsf T}y:y\in\mathbb{R}^m\}\), and \(\mathbb{R}^n_+=\{w:w_i\geq0\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional homogeneous systems; positivity is componentwise and strict positivity means membership in the interior of the nonnegative orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A row-space sign certificate for the infeasibility of \(Ax=0,\ x>0\) is a vector \[w=A^{\mathsf T}y\in\mathcal R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap\bigl(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\}\bigr)\] for some \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\). The certificate set is \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A):=\mathcal R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap\bigl(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\}\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A row-space sign certificate is a nonzero componentwise-nonnegative vector in the row space of \(A\). Thus it has the form \(w=A^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\), with \(w\neq0\). Its sign is incompatible with a strictly positive null vector: if \(Ax=0\) and \(x>0\), then \(w^{\mathsf T}x=0\), whereas every nonzero \(w\geq0\) has \(w^{\mathsf T}x>0\). The definition records the witness itself, not merely the assertion that the positive-kernel system is infeasible. Stiemke's transposition theorem identifies emptiness of this certificate set with existence of a strictly positive vector in \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A)=\{A^{\mathsf T}y:y\in\mathbb{R}^m,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\geq0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\neq0\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A)\neq\varnothing\iff \exists y\in\mathbb{R}^m:\ A^{\mathsf T}y\geq0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y\neq0.\]
By Stiemke's theorem, \[\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A)=\varnothing\iff \exists x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\ Ax=0,\ x>0.\]
special_cases_latex: If \(A^{\mathsf T}y>0\), then the witness is a strict row-space sign certificate and excludes every nonzero \(x\geq0\) in \(\ker A\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The certificate is invariant under positive rescaling: if \(w\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A)\) and \(t>0\), then \(tw\in\mathcal C_{\mathrm{row}}(A)\).
boundary_notes: The zero vector is excluded because it supplies no sign contradiction.
A merely nonnegative certificate need not exclude a boundary null vector \(x\geq0\) whose support is disjoint from that of the certificate.

notation.meaning: every component of x is strictly positive

children.title: Positivity Boundary Regimes
children.top_down_role: Boundary between strictly positive and merely nonnegative alternatives.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Strict, Boundary, and Trivial Positive-Kernel Regimes
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(K_A:=\ker A\cap\mathbb{R}^n_+\), and \(K_A^{++}:=\ker A\cap\mathbb{R}^n_{++}\), where \(\mathbb{R}^n_{++}=\{x:x_i>0\ \forall i\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional homogeneous feasibility; the definition separates interior positivity from nonzero feasibility on the boundary of the orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The positivity regime of \(A\) is defined by the mutually exclusive classification \[\begin{aligned}\mathrm{Strict}(A)&:\ K_A^{++}\neq\varnothing,\\ \mathrm{Boundary}(A)&:\ K_A^{++}=\varnothing\ \text{and}\ K_A\setminus\{0\}\neq\varnothing,\\ \mathrm{Trivial}(A)&:\ K_A=\{0\}.\end{aligned}\] In the boundary regime, every nonzero nonnegative null vector belongs to \(\partial\mathbb{R}^n_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict regime occurs when the kernel of \(A\) contains a vector with every component positive. The boundary regime occurs when the kernel contains a nonzero nonnegative vector but no strictly positive vector. The trivial regime occurs when the only nonnegative null vector is zero. These three cases distinguish the open orthant from its boundary and are exhaustive. Stiemke's alternative associates failure of strict positivity with a nonzero nonnegative row-space vector, while Gordan's homogeneous alternative associates absence of every nonzero nonnegative null vector with a strictly positive row-space vector. Consequently, the boundary regime is precisely the intermediate case in which a weak sign certificate exists but no strict sign certificate exists.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathrm{Boundary}(A)\iff \bigl(\ker A\cap\mathbb{R}^n_{++}=\varnothing\bigr)\ \land\ \bigl(\ker A\cap(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\})\neq\varnothing\bigr).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Using the strict alternatives, \[\mathrm{Boundary}(A)\iff \mathcal R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\})\neq\varnothing\quad\text{and}\quad \mathcal R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap\mathbb{R}^n_{++}=\varnothing.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(n=1\), the boundary regime is empty because every nonzero nonnegative scalar is strictly positive.
immediate_consequences_latex: In the strict regime no nonzero nonnegative row-space sign certificate exists.
In the trivial regime a strictly positive row-space certificate exists.
boundary_notes: Nonzero is essential in the definition of \(K_A\setminus\{0\}\), since zero lies in every kernel.
The classification concerns feasibility, not uniqueness or normalization of positive null vectors.

notation.meaning: strictly positive part of the kernel of A

source_refs.locator: Section 5.6, Propositions 5.6.1 and 5.6.3 and Figure 5.6.2, pp. 210-214

knowledge_statements.title: Unit-Margin Normalization of Strict Positivity
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear range meets the open positive orthant exactly when it contains a vector at least one in every coordinate, reducing strict positivity to ordinary linear programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m\ge1\),
\[\exists x\in\mathbb R^n\; Ax>0\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists z\in\mathbb R^n\; Az\ge\mathbf1_m.\]
Thus strict range positivity can be tested through the ordinary linear-feasibility system \(Az\ge\mathbf1_m\). For rational \(A\), this test has polynomial bit complexity.
assumptions_latex: The polynomial bit-complexity conclusion assumes rational matrix entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\,(Ax>0)\iff\exists z\,(Az\ge\mathbf1_m).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional normalization converting strict componentwise positivity into a nonstrict linear feasibility system.

knowledge_statements.title: Strict-Positivity Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear range contains a strictly positive vector exactly when its orthogonal complement contains no nonzero nonnegative vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(L=\operatorname{range}A\). The strict-positivity regime is \(L\cap\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m}\ne\varnothing\). By the finite-dimensional strict alternative, precisely one of the systems
\[Ax>0\]
and
\[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad y\ge0,\qquad y\ne0\]
has a solution. Thus failure of strict positivity is certified by a nonzero nonnegative vector orthogonal to \(L\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(Ax>0\) for some \(x\in\mathbb{R}^n\), or \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\) for some \(0\ne y\ge0\), is feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Gordan alternative governing intersection with the open positive orthant.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.title: Simplex Normalization of Boundary Feasibility
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Boundary-nonnegative feasibility is equivalent to the range of A meeting the standard simplex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\Delta_m=\{z\in\mathbb R_+^m:\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}z=1\}\), \[\exists x\;(Ax\ge0,\ Ax\ne0)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists u\;(Au\in\Delta_m)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\operatorname{range}A\cap\Delta_m\ne\varnothing.\]
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists x\;(Ax\ge0,\ Ax\ne0)\iff\operatorname{range}A\cap\Delta_m\ne\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous normalization of a nonzero nonnegative image to the standard simplex.

knowledge_statements.title: Boundary-Nonnegativity Regime
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A linear range contains a nonzero nonnegative vector exactly when its orthogonal complement contains no strictly positive vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The boundary-nonnegativity regime is
\[L\cap\bigl(\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\setminus\{0\}\bigr)\ne\varnothing.\]
Precisely one of the systems
\[Ax\ge0,\qquad Ax\ne0\]
and
\[A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad y>0\]
has a solution. Hence a strictly positive vector in \(L^{\perp}\) certifies that \(L\) contains no nonzero nonnegative vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(Ax\ge0\), \(Ax\ne0\), or \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\), \(y>0\), is feasible.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional Stiemke alternative for the closed positive orthant with its origin removed.

notation.meaning: The range of the linear map represented by A.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.title: Support-Face Decomposition of a Boundary Image
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonzero nonnegative image has a unique positive support; proper support means that the image lies on a coordinate boundary rather than in the strictly positive orthant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A vector \(Ax\) is nonzero and nonnegative if and only if, for the nonempty set \(S=\operatorname{supp}_+(Ax)\), \[A_Sx>0,\qquad A_{S^c}x=0.\] The image is strictly positive exactly when \(S=[m]\), and it lies on a proper coordinate face exactly when \(S\subsetneq[m]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Ax\in\mathbb R_+^m\setminus\{0\}\iff\exists\varnothing\ne S\subseteq[m]:A_Sx>0,\ A_{S^c}x=0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decomposition of a nonzero nonnegative image according to its positive and zero coordinates.

notation.meaning: The submatrix of A formed by rows indexed by S.
The indices of the strictly positive coordinates of z.

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonzero nullspace vector can satisfy the weak system without producing a nonzero nonnegative image, so nontriviality must be imposed on Ax rather than on x.

knowledge_statements.title: Positivity-Regime Transition
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict positivity implies nonzero nonnegativity, but a feasible boundary vector may have zero coordinates and need not yield strict positivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because
\[\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m}\subsetneq\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\setminus\{0\},\]
strict positivity of a vector in \(L\) implies boundary nonnegativity. The reverse implication fails: for \(L=\operatorname{span}\{e_1\}\subset\mathbb{R}^{m}\) with \(m\ge2\), the vector \(e_1\) is nonzero and nonnegative, but every vector in \(L\) has zero coordinates and hence none is strictly positive. The transition therefore changes both feasibility and the corresponding alternative certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L\cap\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m}\ne\varnothing\) implies \(L\cap(\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\), while the converse can fail.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares the open-orthant and punctured closed-orthant feasibility regimes.

children.title: Motzkin Transposition Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Unified alternatives for mixed strict and nonstrict linear systems.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^q\). All vector inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine systems containing both strict and nonstrict inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A member of the Motzkin transposition family consists of a mixed primal system and its transposed multiplier conditions. Multipliers attached to strict rows are denoted by \(\mu\); those attached to closed rows are denoted by \(\nu\). Both are nonnegative and their transposed row combination must vanish. Feasibility requires nonnegative pairing with the right-hand sides for every equilibrium multiplier, with strict positivity whenever at least one multiplier of a strict row is nonzero. Equivalently, infeasibility is witnessed by an equilibrium multiplier whose right-hand-side pairing is negative, or whose pairing is zero while \(\mu\neq0\). This distinction is the defining feature that is lost if strict and nonstrict rows are treated identically.
special_cases_latex: If \(p=0\), the family reduces to a nonstrict Farkas alternative.
If \(q=0\), it reduces to a strict affine Gordan alternative.
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive rescaling of a nonzero multiplier certificate preserves certification.
boundary_notes: Replacing \(Ax<b\) by \(Ax\leq b\) changes the strict multiplier clause.
Zero-dimensional row blocks are allowed and encode the named specializations.

notation.meaning: multipliers for strict and nonstrict rows, respectively

children.title: Mixed Strict-Nonstrict Systems
children.top_down_role: Systems combining open and closed halfspace constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Margin Linear-Programming Test
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maximizing a common strictness margin reduces mixed-system feasibility to ordinary linear programming; rational instances are decidable in polynomial bit complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider
\[\sup_{x\in\mathbb R^n,\ t\in\mathbb R}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax+t\mathbf1_p\le b,\qquad Bx\le c.\]
The system \(Ax<b,\ Bx\le c\) is feasible if and only if a feasible pair has \(t>0\), equivalently if the displayed program has positive optimal value or is unbounded above. For rational data, this is an ordinary linear-programming feasibility test with polynomial bit complexity.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^q\).
The polynomial bit-complexity conclusion assumes rational data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists x\,(Ax<b,\ Bx\le c)\iff \exists(x,t)\,(t>0,\ Ax+t\mathbf1_p\le b,\ Bx\le c).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional feasibility test for a mixed strict-nonstrict system using one common margin variable.

notation.meaning: All-ones vector for the strict constraint block.
Common margin for the strict inequalities.

knowledge_statements.title: Convexity and Closure of a Feasible Mixed System
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed feasible set is convex. If nonempty, its closure is obtained by relaxing its strict inequalities; the closure identity can fail when the mixed system is empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let
\[F:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax<b,\ Bx\le c\},\qquad \widehat F:=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:Ax\le b,\ Bx\le c\}.\]
Then \(F\) is convex. If \(F\ne\varnothing\), then \(\overline F=\widehat F\). The nonemptiness assumption is essential: an empty strict system may have a nonempty closed relaxation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is convex, and }F\ne\varnothing\Longrightarrow \overline F=\{x:Ax\le b,\ Bx\le c\}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexity and ambient closure of a nonempty finite-dimensional mixed feasible set.

notation.meaning: Feasible set of the mixed strict-nonstrict system.
Closed relaxation of the strict block.

knowledge_statements.title: Mixed Strict-Nonstrict Systems
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed system requires one vector to satisfy the strict block Ax<b and the nonstrict block Bx≤c simultaneously; either block may be empty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mixed strict-nonstrict system is
\[Ax<b,\qquad Bx\le c.\]
Its feasible set is the intersection of the open halfspaces specified by the rows of \(A\) and \(b\) with the closed halfspaces specified by the rows of \(B\) and \(c\). Either block may be empty, yielding a purely strict or purely nonstrict system.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed system is feasible exactly when there exists \(x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\) satisfying \(Ax<b\) and \(Bx\le c\) componentwise.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine systems with one open and one closed block of halfspace constraints.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^q\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional affine feasibility with separately indexed open and closed halfspace constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed strict-nonstrict linear system is the feasible-set specification \[F_{<,\leq}(A,B;b,c):=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\ (i=1,\ldots,p),\ b_j^{\mathsf T}x\leq c_j\ (j=1,\ldots,q)\},\] equivalently \[F_{<,\leq}(A,B;b,c)=\{x:Ax<b,\ Bx\leq c\}.\] The strict block is an intersection of open halfspaces, whereas the nonstrict block is an intersection of closed halfspaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed strict-nonstrict system combines finitely many strict affine inequalities with finitely many nonstrict affine inequalities in the same decision vector. The rows of \(A\) define the strict block \(Ax<b\); the rows of \(B\) define the closed block \(Bx\leq c\). The two row blocks remain distinguished because their transposition certificates obey different zero-pairing rules. The system is feasible when its defined set is nonempty and infeasible when that set is empty. Empty row blocks are permitted, so the definition includes purely strict and purely nonstrict systems without changing notation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[F_{<,\leq}(A,B;b,c)=\bigcap_{i=1}^{p}\{x:a_i^{\mathsf T}x<b_i\}\cap\bigcap_{j=1}^{q}\{x:b_j^{\mathsf T}x\leq c_j\}.\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: Introducing a common strict slack gives \[F_{<,\leq}\neq\varnothing\iff \exists(x,t):Ax+t\mathbf1\leq b,\ Bx\leq c,\ t>0.\]
special_cases_latex: For \(p=0\), the feasible set is the polyhedron \(\{x:Bx\leq c\}\).
For \(q=0\), it is an intersection of open halfspaces \(\{x:Ax<b\}\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The feasible set is convex, although it need not be closed when \(p>0\).
boundary_notes: The componentwise relation \(<\) requires every strict row to have positive slack.
Closure generally replaces strict rows by nonstrict rows only under additional nonemptiness and accessibility conditions.

notation.meaning: all-ones vector of the dimension of the strict block

children.title: Transposition Certificates
children.top_down_role: Multiplier witnesses associated with mixed inequality systems.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Nontriviality Boundaries
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The nontriviality disjunction is essential: deleting it lets zero multipliers certify every system, while requiring a nonzero strict-block multiplier would reject valid pure-nonstrict certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If the nontriviality disjunction is deleted, \((y,z)=(0,0)\) satisfies \[y,z\ge0,\qquad A^{\mathsf T}y+B^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z\le0\] for every system, including feasible systems. Conversely, the disjunction cannot be replaced by \(y\ne0\): when \(p=0\), the infeasible inequality \(0\le-1\) has the certificate \(z=1\), for which \(c^{\mathsf T}z=-1<0\).
assumptions_latex: Use the mixed-system notation \(Ax<b\), \(Bx\le c\) with \(y\in\mathbb R_+^p\) and \(z\in\mathbb R_+^q\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The condition \(y\ne0\) or \(b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z<0\) can neither be omitted nor replaced by \(y\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: This records both sharp roles of the certificate disjunction: excluding the universal zero pair and retaining pure-nonstrict Farkas certificates.

knowledge_statements.title: Certificate Normalization Dichotomy
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every Motzkin certificate can be positively rescaled so that either its right-hand-side value is minus one, or that value is zero and its strict-block multipliers sum to one; either normal form is sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s=b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z\). The Motzkin certificate conditions are equivalently \[y\ge0,\quad z\ge0,\quad A^{\mathsf T}y+B^{\mathsf T}z=0,\] together with one of the alternatives \[s=-1,\qquad\text{or}\qquad s=0\ \text{ and }\ \mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}y=1.\]
assumptions_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb R^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^p\), and \(c\in\mathbb R^q\), and set \(s=b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax<b,\ Bx\le c\) is infeasible if and only if nonnegative \(y,z\) satisfy the transposed balance equation and either \(s=-1\), or \(s=0\) and \(\mathbf 1^{\mathsf T}y=1\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive rescaling yields two canonical branches: negative scalar value normalized to minus one, or zero scalar value with the nonzero nonnegative strict-block multipliers normalized to unit sum.

notation.meaning: Scalar value of the multipliers on the right-hand sides.

knowledge_statements.title: Transposition Certificates
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mixed system is infeasible exactly when nonnegative strict-block and nonstrict-block multipliers cancel its variable coefficients, give a nonpositive scalar bound, and obtain strictness from either a nonzero strict-block multiplier or a strictly negative bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The mixed system \(Ax<b\), \(Bx\le c\) is infeasible if and only if there exist multipliers \(y\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p}\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{q}\) satisfying
\[A^{\mathsf T}y+B^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z\le0,\]
and
\[y\ne0\quad\text{or}\quad b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z<0.\]
Such a pair \((y,z)\) is a Motzkin transposition certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The system \(Ax<b\), \(Bx\le c\) is infeasible if and only if there exist \(y\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p}\) and \(z\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{q}\) such that \(A^{\mathsf T}y+B^{\mathsf T}z=0\), \(b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z\le0\), and either \(y\ne0\) or \(b^{\mathsf T}y+c^{\mathsf T}z<0\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Motzkin multiplier certificate using the strict-block nontriviality disjunction.

notation.meaning: Nonnegative multiplier for the strict block.
Nonnegative multiplier for the nonstrict block.

knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A,B,b,c\) define the mixed system \(Ax<b,\ Bx\leq c\), with dimensions as in Motzkin's theorem.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional exact infeasibility certificates for mixed affine inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A transposition certificate is a nonnegative multiplier pair whose weighted row normals cancel. Its weighted right-hand side is nonpositive. If that value is zero, at least one multiplier belonging to a strict inequality must be nonzero; if the value is negative, the nonstrict block alone may supply the contradiction. This disjunction prevents the zero multiplier pair from being counted as a certificate and exactly reflects the difference between strict and closed constraints. Motzkin's theorem states that the mixed primal system is infeasible exactly when this certificate set is nonempty.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The nontriviality clause may be written \[s<0\quad\text{or}\quad(s=0\ \text{and}\ \mu\neq0).\]
Motzkin's alternative gives \[\operatorname{Cert}_M(A,B;b,c)\neq\varnothing\iff\{x:Ax<b,\ Bx\leq c\}=\varnothing.\]

For homogeneous right-hand sides, certification requires \(A^{\mathsf T}\mu+B^{\mathsf T}
u=0\) with \((\mu,
u)\geq0\) and \(\mu
eq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Every positive multiple of a transposition certificate is again a certificate.
boundary_notes: A pair with \(\mu=0\) and zero right-hand-side pairing is not a certificate, even if \(\nu\neq0\).

children.title: Motzkin Specialization Map
children.top_down_role: Organization of Farkas, Gordan, and strict-inequality alternatives as special regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Affine Strict-Inequality Specialization
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting the nonstrict block gives the affine strict-inequality alternative; setting its right-hand side to zero further specializes it to Gordan's theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\), exactly one of the systems \[\exists x\in\mathbb{R}^{n}:Ax<b\] and \[\exists y\in\mathbb{R}^{p}_{+}\setminus\{0\}:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\quad b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\] is feasible. Setting \(b=0\) gives the homogeneous Gordan form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exactly one of \(\exists x:Ax<b\) and \(\exists y\ge0,\ y\ne0,\ A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ b^{\mathsf T}y\le0\) holds.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Motzkin specialization obtained by deleting the nonstrict block while retaining an arbitrary strict-block right-hand side.

knowledge_statements.title: Motzkin Specialization Map
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deleting the nonstrict block and homogenizing the strict right-hand side gives Gordan's alternative; deleting the strict block gives the affine Farkas alternative.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the mixed system \(Ax<b\), \(Bx\le c\), deleting the nonstrict block and setting \(b=0\) gives
\[Ax<0\quad\text{versus}\quad A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\qquad 0\ne y\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{p},\]
which is a sign-equivalent form of Gordan's theorem. Deleting the strict block gives
\[Bx\le c\quad\text{versus}\quad B^{\mathsf T}z=0,\qquad z\in\mathbb{R}_{+}^{q},\qquad c^{\mathsf T}z<0,\]
the corresponding Farkas infeasibility alternative. Thus block deletion and a zero strict-block right-hand side provide the specialization map.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{p\times n}\), \(B\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^{p}\), and \(c\in\mathbb{R}^{q}\), with the usual conventions for empty constraint blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Deleting the nonstrict block and setting \(b=0\) yields the homogeneous strict Gordan alternative, while deleting the strict block yields the affine nonstrict Farkas alternative.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Specializations use deletion of constraint blocks and homogeneous right-hand sides.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(M(A,B;b,c)\) denote the Motzkin pair consisting of \(Ax<b,\ Bx\leq c\) and its transposed multiplier conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A formal map between finite-dimensional alternative systems obtained by deleting or homogenizing constraint blocks.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The specialization map records how Motzkin's mixed alternative reduces when a row block is absent or the right-hand sides are homogenized. Deleting the strict block yields the usual nonstrict Farkas infeasibility multiplier, which must have a strictly negative right-hand-side pairing. Deleting the nonstrict block yields the strict affine Gordan alternative, where a nonzero strict-block multiplier may have zero pairing. Setting both right-hand sides to zero yields the homogeneous mixed alternative, in which nontriviality must occur in the strict multiplier block. Further sign changes, equality splitting, or slack-variable lifts produce familiar Farkas, Gordan, and Stiemke orientations without altering the underlying transposed equilibrium relation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\mathfrak S_M:\ (A,B;b,c)\mapsto\text{the reduced primal/certificate pair obtained by block deletion or }(b,c)=(0,0).\]
equivalent_formulations_latex: The strict homogeneous specialization is \[Ax<0\text{ infeasible}\iff\exists\mu\geq0,\ \mu\neq0:\ A^{\mathsf T}\mu=0.\]
special_cases_latex: Stiemke's homogeneous system is obtained by expressing \(Ax=0,\ x>0\) as \(-x<0,\ Ax\leq0,\ -Ax\leq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: The multiplier dimensions shrink with the deleted row block, while the decision-space dimension remains \(n\).
boundary_notes: Deleting a block is distinct from retaining it with zero rows.
Strict and nonstrict blocks cannot generally be interchanged because their zero-pairing clauses differ.

children.title: Linear Alternative Duality Map
children.top_down_role: Transpose, orthogonal-complement, homogenization, and specialization relationships among named alternatives.

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let a linear alternative system have row matrix \(R\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), right-hand side \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and a specified product cone \(Q\subseteq\mathbb{R}^m\) for admissible multipliers.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear alternatives; strict-row information is retained as part of the system signature.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The linear-alternative duality map is \[\mathfrak D:(R,r,Q)\longmapsto\{y\in Q:R^{\mathsf T}y=0\}\times\{r^{\mathsf T}y:y\in Q,\ R^{\mathsf T}y=0\}.\] For a Motzkin signature \(R=[A;B]\), \(r=(b,c)\), and \(Q=\mathbb{R}^p_+\times\mathbb{R}^q_+\), the map retains the distinguished strict block and returns \[A^{\mathsf T}\mu+B^{\mathsf T}\nu=0,\qquad b^{\mathsf T}\mu+c^{\mathsf T}\nu.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The duality map sends row constraints to nonnegative multiplier equilibria in the transposed space and pairs each equilibrium with the original right-hand side. Transposition produces the cancellation condition; the scalar pairing determines whether a multiplier is compatible with primal feasibility or certifies infeasibility. For mixed systems, the map also records which multiplier coordinates correspond to strict rows, since zero pairing is contradictory only when the strict multiplier block is nonzero. Orthogonal-complement descriptions, homogenization, sign reversal, and named theorem specializations are representations of this same transpose-and-pairing construction.
equivalent_formulations_latex: The equilibrium condition is \((\mu,\nu)\in\ker[A^{\mathsf T}\ B^{\mathsf T}]\cap(\mathbb{R}^p_+\times\mathbb{R}^q_+)\).
For homogeneous systems, the scalar pairing vanishes and the alternative is determined by the permitted nonzero multiplier blocks.
special_cases_latex: For an equality system \(Ax=b\), unrestricted multipliers give the orthogonal-complement condition \(A^{\mathsf T}y=0\).
For a cone-membership system \(b=S\lambda,\ \lambda\geq0\), the map yields polar vectors satisfying \(S^{\mathsf T}y\leq0\).
immediate_consequences_latex: Positive scaling of an admissible multiplier scales the pairing without changing its sign.
boundary_notes: The map alone does not choose the strict nontriviality clause; that clause belongs to the source system's signature.
Transpose depends on the chosen Euclidean pairing.

children.title: Gordan-Stiemke Dual Orientation
children.top_down_role: Transpose and orthogonal-complement relationship between strict alternative families.

knowledge_statements.title: Gordan-Stiemke Dual Orientation
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transpose kernels are orthogonal complements of ranges, so Gordan and Stiemke exchange strict and boundary positivity across this orthogonality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Since
\[(\operatorname{range}A)^{\perp}=\ker A^{\mathsf T},\]
the Gordan orientation pairs strict positivity in \(\operatorname{range}A\) with nonzero nonnegativity in \(\ker A^{\mathsf T}\):
\[\operatorname{range}A\cap\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m}=\varnothing
\iff
\ker A^{\mathsf T}\cap\bigl(\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\setminus\{0\}\bigr)\ne\varnothing.\]
The Stiemke orientation exchanges the cone regimes, pairing a nonzero nonnegative range vector with exclusion of a strictly positive vector from the transpose kernel.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{range}A\cap\mathbb{R}_{++}^{m}=\varnothing\) iff \(\ker A^{\mathsf T}\cap(\mathbb{R}_{+}^{m}\setminus\{0\})\ne\varnothing\), with the strict and boundary cones exchanged in the Stiemke orientation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Orthogonal-complement formulation of the finite-dimensional Gordan and Stiemke alternatives.

source_witnesses.locator: 4.1 Separation Between Convex Sets p. 121

knowledge_statements.slot_contract: State the canonical mathematical definition of the source node, with its domain, quantifiers, notation, and a precise source locator.
knowledge_statements.ambient_context_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(N(A)=\ker A\), and \(R(A^{\mathsf T})=\operatorname{range}(A^{\mathsf T})=N(A)^{\perp}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Homogeneous finite-dimensional alternatives under the standard Euclidean inner product.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Gordan-Stiemke dual orientation is the paired classification \[\begin{aligned}\text{Gordan orientation: }&N(A)\cap(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing\iff R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap\mathbb{R}^n_{++}\neq\varnothing,\\ \text{Stiemke orientation: }&N(A)\cap\mathbb{R}^n_{++}\neq\varnothing\iff R(A^{\mathsf T})\cap(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\})=\varnothing.\end{aligned}\] The orientation map exchanges kernel with orthogonal row space and exchanges strict positivity with nonzero nonnegativity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual orientation places kernel feasibility and row-space certification on opposite sides of the Euclidean orthogonal-complement relation. In the Gordan orientation, absence of every nonzero nonnegative null vector is certified by a strictly positive row-space vector. In the Stiemke orientation, existence of a strictly positive null vector is equivalent to absence of every nonzero nonnegative row-space vector. The two orientations differ only in which side receives strict positivity, but that difference controls the boundary regime of the orthant.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[N(A)^{\perp}=R(A^{\mathsf T}),\qquad \mathbb{R}^n_{++}=\operatorname{int}\mathbb{R}^n_+,\] together with the two displayed alternatives defines the orientation.
equivalent_formulations_latex: Stiemke's orientation may be written \[\exists x>0:\ Ax=0\iff\bigl(A^{\mathsf T}y\geq0\Rightarrow A^{\mathsf T}y=0\bigr).\]
Gordan's orientation may be written \[\exists y:\ A^{\mathsf T}y>0\iff\bigl(Ax=0,\ x\geq0\Rightarrow x=0\bigr).\]
special_cases_latex: If \(A=0\), Stiemke feasibility holds and the row space is \(\{0\}\).
If \(A\) has full column rank, the nonnegative kernel is trivial and Gordan's strict row-space certificate exists.
immediate_consequences_latex: The boundary regime occurs exactly when the row space meets \(\mathbb{R}^n_+\setminus\{0\}\) but not \(\mathbb{R}^n_{++}\).
boundary_notes: Strict positivity cannot be replaced by nonnegativity on both sides without destroying exclusivity.
